Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) 
Patient Admission Process 
For Hospital Operations & Insurance/TPA Coordination (Medi Assist 
Compatible) 
Document Type: Admission Management SOP 
Version: 1.0 
Effective Date: 01-Jan-2026 
Department: Admissions / Front Office / Insurance Desk 
Review Frequency: Annual 
 
1. Purpose 
To establish a standardized process for admitting patients into the hospital while ensuring: 
• Accurate patient registration  
• Regulatory compliance  
• Timely clinical assessment  
• Insurance verification  
• Cashless authorization initiation  
• Proper documentation  
• Positive patient experience  
Patient admission serves as the formal entry point into inpatient care and must include

Patient admission serves as the formal entry point into inpatient care and must include 
administrative, clinical, and financial validation before treatment proceeds, except in 
emergency situations.  
 
2. Scope 
This SOP applies to: 
• Front Office  
• Admission Department  
• Insurance / TPA Desk  
• Nursing Department  
• Duty Medical Officer (DMO)  
• Treating Consultants  
• Billing Department  
• Medical Records Department

3. Types of Admissions 
Admission Type Description 
Planned Admission Scheduled hospitalization 
Emergency Admission Immediate admission due to urgent medical condition 
Day Care Admission Procedures requiring short stay 
Surgical Admission Admission for planned surgery 
Maternity Admission Obstetric care and delivery 
Transfer Admission Patient transferred from another facility 
 
4. Roles and Responsibilities 
Front Office Executive 
Responsible for: 
• Patient registration  
• Identity verification  
• Document collection  
• Admission form completion  
 
Insurance Coordinator 
Responsible for: 
• Policy verification  
• Cashless initiation  
• TPA coordination  
• Pre-authorization submission  
 
Duty Doctor 
Responsible for: 
• Medical assessment  
• Admission recommendation

Duty Doctor 
Responsible for: 
• Medical assessment  
• Admission recommendation  
• Initial treatment orders

Nursing Team 
Responsible for: 
• Bed allocation coordination  
• Initial patient assessment  
• Admission checklist completion  
 
5. Admission Workflow 
Patient Arrival 
      │ 
      ▼ 
Registration 
      │ 
      ▼

      ▼

      ▼

      ▼ 
Bed Allocation

      ▼

      ▼

      ▼

6. Planned Admission Procedure 
Step 1: Patient Arrival 
Patient presents: 
• Admission advice from consultant  
• Referral letter (if applicable)

• Insurance card  
• Government-issued ID  
Examples: 
• Aadhaar Card  
• Passport  
• Driving License  
• PAN Card  
 
Step 2: Registration 
Create or verify: 
• Unique Hospital Identification Number (UHID)  
• Existing patient record  
• Demographic information  
Capture: 
• Full Name  
• Date of Birth  
• Gender  
• Mobile Number  
• Address  
• Emergency Contact  
 
Step 3: Identity Verification 
Mandatory verification: 
• Name matching  
• Photo identification  
• Insurance card validation  
Any discrepancy must be escalated before admission. 
 
Step 4: Consultant Admission Order 
Admission cannot proceed without: 
• Consultant recommendation

• Admission diagnosis  
• Planned treatment  
The admission note should document the reason for admission, patient status, clinical 
findings, and initial care plan.  
 
Step 5: Bed Allocation 
Admission Department shall: 
• Verify bed availability  
• Assign ward category  
• Confirm room eligibility under insurance  
Categories: 
• General Ward  
• Semi-Private  
• Private Room  
• Deluxe Room  
• ICU  
• HDU  
 
7. Insurance & Cashless Admission Process 
Eligibility Verification 
Insurance Desk shall verify: 
• Policy status  
• Coverage period  
• Sum insured  
• Network eligibility  
• Waiting periods  
• Exclusions  
 
Required Documents 
Collect: 
• Insurance Card

• Government ID  
• Employee ID (if corporate policy)  
• Doctor admission advice  
 
Cashless Intimation 
Submit to Medi Assist: 
• Pre-Authorization Form  
• Clinical Notes  
• Investigation Reports  
• Cost Estimate  
Timeline: 
• Within 2 hours of admission request  
 
8. Emergency Admission Procedure 
Definition 
Admission required to prevent: 
• Loss of life  
• Organ damage  
• Clinical deterioration  
Examples: 
• Stroke  
• Heart Attack  
• Major Trauma  
• Respiratory Failure  
 
Emergency Workflow 
Immediate Treatment 
Medical care must begin immediately. 
Insurance approval shall not delay treatment.

Registration 
Registration should be completed after stabilization if necessary. 
 
Insurance Notification 
Insurance desk must notify TPA: 
• Within 24 hours of admission  
 
9. Admission Documentation Checklist 
Administrative Documents 
• Admission Form  
• Consent Form  
• Patient Rights Acknowledgement  
• Identity Proof  
• Insurance Documents  
 
Clinical Documents 
• Admission Note  
• Initial Assessment  
• Consultant Orders  
• Medication Orders  
• Nursing Assessment  
Admission documentation forms the baseline medical record for subsequent treatment and 
inpatient management.  
 
10. Consent Management 
General Admission Consent 
Must include:

• Consent for treatment  
• Diagnostic procedures  
• Information sharing  
• Billing acknowledgment  
 
Special Consents 
Required separately for: 
• Surgery  
• Blood Transfusion  
• ICU Admission  
• High-Risk Procedures  
• Anaesthesia  
 
11. Financial Counseling 
Patient shall be informed regarding: 
• Estimated treatment cost  
• Advance deposit  
• Insurance limitations  
• Non-payable items  
• Co-pay obligations  
Documentation of financial counseling is mandatory. 
 
12. Patient Rights & Responsibilities 
Patient must receive information regarding: 
Rights 
• Privacy  
• Confidentiality  
• Informed consent  
• Access to medical information  
• Respectful treatment  
Responsibilities

• Accurate information disclosure  
• Compliance with treatment  
• Financial obligations  
• Following hospital policies  
 
13. Admission Completion Checklist 
Before transferring patient to ward: 
Item Status 
Registration Complete ✓ 
UHID Generated ✓ 
Identity Verified ✓ 
Admission Order Available ✓ 
Bed Assigned ✓ 
Consent Obtained ✓ 
Insurance Initiated ✓ 
Advance Collected (if applicable) ✓ 
Clinical Assessment Done ✓ 
 
14. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) 
KPI Target 
Registration Time ≤ 10 Minutes 
Admission Completion ≤ 30 Minutes 
Insurance Verification ≤ 20 Minutes 
Bed Allocation ≤ 15 Minutes 
Documentation Completeness > 98% 
Admission Errors < 1%

Admission Executive 
Level 2

Admission Supervisor 
Level 3 
Operations Manager 
Level 4 
Hospital Administrator 
Level 5 
Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Appendix B – Sample Admission Scenarios 
for RAG 
Scenario 1 
Question: What documents are required for cashless admission? 
Answer: Insurance card, government ID, admission advice, policy details, and pre-

Answer: Insurance card, government ID, admission advice, policy details, and pre-
authorization form.

Scenario 2 
Question: Can treatment start before insurance approval in emergencies? 
Answer: Yes. Emergency treatment must not be delayed for insurance authorization. 
Scenario 3 
Question: Who is responsible for bed allocation? 
Answer: Admission Department in coordination with Nursing and Operations.

HOSPITAL COMPLIANCE & 
REGULATORY MANUAL 
Administrator Reference Dataset 
Version: 1.0 
Document Owner: Quality & Compliance Department 
Applicable To: Hospital Administrators, Compliance Officers, Quality Managers, Medical 
Superintendents 
 
SECTION 1: NABH COMPLIANCE 
GUIDELINES SUMMARY 
Purpose 
To establish standards for patient safety, quality healthcare delivery, risk management, 
documentation, and operational excellence. 
 
Key NABH Compliance Areas 
1. Access, Assessment & Continuity of Care 
Requirements: 
• Defined admission process 
• Patient assessment protocols 
• Continuity of care documentation 
• Referral management 
Administrator Responsibilities: 
• Monitor admission turnaround times 
• Ensure assessment compliance 
• Maintain referral records 
 
2. Care of Patients

• Ensure assessment compliance 
• Maintain referral records 
 
2. Care of Patients 
Requirements:

• Clinical care pathways 
• Treatment documentation 
• High-risk patient management 
Administrator Controls: 
• Clinical audit reviews 
• Incident monitoring 
• Outcome reporting 
 
3. Medication Management 
Requirements: 
• Safe prescribing 
• Medication reconciliation 
• High-alert medication controls 
Compliance Indicators: 
• Medication error rate 
• Adverse drug events 
• Pharmacy audits 
 
4. Patient Rights & Education 
Patients have rights to: 
• Information 
• Privacy 
• Confidentiality 
• Informed consent 
• Safe treatment 
• Complaint resolution 
Administrator Responsibilities: 
• Display patient rights 
• Monitor grievance handling 
• Track consent compliance 
 
5. Infection Control

Requirements: 
• Hand hygiene programs 
• Isolation procedures 
• Biomedical waste management 
• HAI surveillance 
KPIs: 
• CAUTI Rate 
• CLABSI Rate 
• SSI Rate 
 
6. Information Management System 
Requirements: 
• Medical record security 
• Record retention 
• Access controls 
• Audit trails 
Administrator Responsibilities: 
• EHR governance 
• Data protection monitoring 
• Backup verification 
 
SECTION 2: HIPAA SUMMARY FOR 
HEALTHCARE ADMINISTRATORS 
Purpose 
Protect patient health information and regulate disclosure of healthcare data. 
 
Protected Health Information (PHI) 
Examples: 
• Patient Name 
• Medical Record Number

• Diagnosis 
• Insurance Details 
• Laboratory Reports 
• Treatment Information 
 
HIPAA Privacy Principles 
Access only when: 
• Required for treatment 
• Required for operations 
• Required for payment processing 
Prohibited: 
• Unauthorized sharing 
• Social media disclosure 
• Personal email transmission 
 
Minimum Necessary Rule 
Employees may access only: 
• Information needed for assigned duties 
Examples: 
Billing Staff: 
Access billing records only 
Nursing Staff: 
Access assigned patient records only 
 
Breach Management 
Potential Breach Examples: 
• Lost laptop 
• Misdirected email 
• Unauthorized access 
• Stolen patient records

Administrator Actions: 
1. Investigate incident 
2. Notify compliance officer 
3. Document findings 
4. Implement corrective actions 
 
SECTION 3: DATA PRIV ACY POLICY 
Objective 
Protect personal and health information collected by the hospital. 
 
Data Categories 
Patient Data 
• Demographics 
• Clinical records 
• Diagnostic reports 
• Insurance information 
Employee Data 
• Payroll records 
• Credentials 
• Performance records 
Vendor Data 
• Contracts 
• Financial information 
 
Data Collection Principles 
The hospital shall collect only: 
• Necessary information 
• Lawfully obtained information 
• Purpose-specific information

Data Storage Requirements 
Electronic Records: 
• Encryption mandatory 
• Role-based access 
• Audit logging enabled 
Physical Records: 
• Locked storage 
• Controlled access 
 
Data Sharing Rules 
Allowed: 
• Treating physicians 
• Insurance partners 
• Regulatory authorities 
Prohibited: 
• Unauthorized third parties 
• Personal devices 
• Unapproved cloud storage 
 
Data Retention Schedule 
Record Type Retention 
Medical Records 10 Years 
Claims Records 10 Years 
Billing Records 8 Years 
HR Records 7 Years 
 
Data Disposal 
Electronic: 
• Secure deletion

• Storage sanitization 
Physical: 
• Cross-cut shredding 
• Authorized destruction 
 
SECTION 4: PATIENT CONSENT 
POLICY 
Purpose 
Ensure patients provide informed authorization before treatment. 
 
Consent Categories 
General Consent 
Obtained during admission. 
Includes: 
• Examination 
• Routine treatment 
• Nursing care 
 
Informed Consent 
Required for: 
• Surgery 
• Invasive procedures 
• Anaesthesia 
• Blood transfusion 
Consent Must Include: 
• Diagnosis 
• Procedure details 
• Benefits 
• Risks

• Alternatives 
• Consequences of refusal 
 
High-Risk Consent 
Required for: 
• ICU admission 
• Organ support 
• Experimental therapy 
 
Telemedicine Consent 
Required before: 
• Virtual consultation 
• Remote monitoring 
 
Research Consent 
Required before: 
• Clinical trials 
• Research participation 
• Data publication 
 
Consent Validation Rules 
Valid Consent Requires: 
• Patient identification 
• Capacity assessment 
• Voluntary agreement 
• Witness (where applicable) 
• Documentation 
 
Consent Withdrawal

Patients may withdraw consent unless: 
• Emergency treatment required 
• Legal obligations apply 
 
SECTION 5: PATIENT RIGHTS POLICY 
Rights of Patients 
Patients have the right to: 
• Respect and dignity 
• Privacy 
• Confidentiality 
• Safe care 
• Access to information 
• Refuse treatment 
• Obtain second opinion 
• Complaint resolution 
 
Grievance Management 
Complaint Channels: 
• Patient Relations Desk 
• Email 
• Hotline 
• Written Complaint 
Resolution Targets: 
Level 1: 24 Hours 
Level 2: 3 Days 
Level 3: 7 Days 
 
SECTION 6: MEDICAL RECORD 
MANAGEMENT POLICY 
Objectives

Ensure accurate and secure healthcare records. 
 
Medical Record Components 
• Admission Notes 
• Progress Notes 
• Nursing Notes 
• Laboratory Reports 
• Imaging Reports 
• Consent Forms 
• Discharge Summary 
 
Record Completion SLA 
Discharge Summary: 
Within 24 hours of discharge 
Operative Notes: 
Within 12 hours 
Death Summary: 
Within 24 hours 
 
SECTION 7: INCIDENT REPORTING 
POLICY 
Reportable Events 
• Patient fall 
• Medication error 
• Wrong patient identification 
• Data breach 
• Equipment malfunction 
 
Reporting Timeline 
Critical Incident: 
Immediate

Serious Incident: 
Within 2 Hours 
Minor Incident: 
Within 24 Hours 
 
Escalation Matrix 
Level 1: 
Department Manager 
Level 2: 
Quality Manager 
Level 3: 
Medical Superintendent 
Level 4: 
Hospital Administrator 
Level 5: 
Chief Executive Officer 
 
SECTION 8: AUDIT & COMPLIANCE 
MONITORING 
Internal Audits 
Monthly: 
• Documentation Audit 
• Consent Audit 
• Infection Control Audit 
Quarterly: 
• Regulatory Compliance Audit 
• Data Privacy Audit 
Annual: 
• NABH Readiness Assessment

Compliance KPIs 
KPI Target 
Consent Compliance > 98% 
Documentation Completion > 99% 
Privacy Breaches 0 
Incident Reporting Compliance 100% 
Audit Closure Rate > 95%

compliance@hospital.org

privacy@hospital.org

ms@hospital.org

admin@hospital.org 
Emergency Compliance Hotline: 
1800-000-0000 
 
SECTION 10: RAG QA EXAMPLES 
Question: 
What records require informed consent? 
Answer: 
Surgery, invasive procedures, anaesthesia, blood transfusion, high-risk treatment, 
telemedicine, and research participation.

Question: 
Who should receive a data breach report? 
Answer: 
Compliance Officer, Privacy Officer, Department Head, and Hospital Administrator. 
 
Question: 
How long should medical records be retained? 
Answer: 
Medical records should be retained for 10 years. 
 
Question: 
What is the escalation path for a serious compliance incident? 
Answer: 
Department Manager → Quality Manager → Medical Superintendent → Hospital 
Administrator → CEO. 
 
Question: 
What are the patient's core rights? 
Answer: 
Privacy, confidentiality, informed consent, dignity, safe care, information access, treatment 
refusal, and grievance resolution.

Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) 
Hospital Operations & Cashless Claims Management 
For Integration with Medi Assist TPA Services 
Document Type: Hospital SOP 
Version: 1.0 
Effective Date: 01-Jan-2026 
Review Frequency: Annual 
Prepared For: Hospital Network Partners of Medi Assist Healthcare Services 
 
1. Purpose 
This SOP defines the standardized operational procedures for hospitals empaneled with Medi 
Assist for: 
• Cashless hospitalization  
• Pre-authorization processing  
• Emergency admissions  
• Planned admissions  
• Inpatient billing  
• Discharge management  
• Claims submission  
• Query resolution  
• Fraud prevention  
• Record retention  
The objective is to ensure timely patient care, regulatory compliance, accurate claims

The objective is to ensure timely patient care, regulatory compliance, accurate claims 
adjudication, and improved patient experience. 
 
2. Scope 
This SOP applies to: 
• Front Office / Admission Desk  
• Insurance Desk / TPA Desk  
• Billing Department  
• Medical Records Department  
• Nursing Department  
• Treating Consultants  
• Finance Department

• Quality & Compliance Team  
 
3. Definitions 
Term Definition 
TPA Third Party Administrator 
Cashless Claim Claim settled directly between insurer/TPA and hospital 
Pre-Authorization Approval sought before treatment costs are incurred 
Enhancement Additional approval request when costs exceed approved amount 
Final Authorization Final approval granted before discharge 
Non-Medical Expenses Expenses not payable under policy terms 
Package Rate Pre-negotiated treatment tariff 
 
4. Roles & Responsibilities 
Insurance Desk Executive 
Responsible for: 
• Policy verification  
• Document collection  
• Pre-auth submission  
• Enhancement requests  
• Communication with Medi Assist  
 
Treating Doctor 
Responsible for: 
• Clinical diagnosis  
• Treatment planning  
• Medical justification

Responsible for: 
• Clinical diagnosis  
• Treatment planning  
• Medical justification  
• Documentation accuracy  
 
Billing Executive 
Responsible for:

• Package mapping  
• Bill preparation  
• Deduction management  
• Final claim submission  
 
Medical Records Officer 
Responsible for: 
• Maintaining patient records  
• Uploading discharge documents  
• Record retention  
 
5. Planned Admission Process 
Step 1: Patient Registration 
Collect: 
• Government ID  
• Health Insurance Card  
• Employee ID (if corporate policy)  
• Doctor's admission advice  
Verify: 
• Patient identity  
• Policy validity  
• Network eligibility  
 
Step 2: Policy Verification 
Insurance Desk shall: 
1. Verify policy through Medi Assist portal.  
2. Confirm:  
o Active coverage  
o Sum insured  
o Waiting periods  
o Exclusions  
o Co-pay clauses

Step 3: Pre-Authorization Submission 
Timeline: 
• Within 2 hours of admission registration.  
Required documents: 
• Pre-auth form  
• Doctor admission notes  
• Investigation reports  
• Insurance card copy  
• KYC documents  
Mandatory fields: 
• Diagnosis  
• Proposed treatment  
• Estimated cost  
• Expected length of stay  
 
Step 4: Approval Monitoring 
Insurance Desk shall: 
• Track approval status every 30 minutes.  
• Respond to TPA queries within 60 minutes.  
• Escalate delays beyond SLA.  
 
6. Emergency Admission Process 
Definition 
Any admission requiring immediate treatment where delay may endanger life or health. 
Examples: 
• Myocardial Infarction  
• Stroke  
• Polytrauma  
• Severe Sepsis

• Acute Respiratory Failure  
 
Procedure 
Immediate Care 
Treatment shall not be delayed for insurance approval. 
Documentation 
Within 24 hours: 
Submit: 
• Emergency certificate  
• Admission notes  
• Clinical findings  
• Investigation reports  
Cashless Intimation 
Notify Medi Assist within: 
• 24 hours from admission  
 
7. Inpatient Monitoring 
Insurance Desk shall review: 
• Daily treatment progress  
• ICU transfers  
• Surgical procedures  
• Cost utilization  
 
Enhancement Request Process 
Enhancement required if: 
• Expected bill exceeds approved amount by ≥10%.  
Submit:

• Updated estimate  
• Progress notes  
• Investigation reports  
• Procedure details  
Timeline: 
• Minimum 24 hours before discharge whenever possible.  
 
8. Surgical Case Management 
Prior to surgery: 
Verify: 
• Procedure code  
• Package eligibility  
• Implant coverage  
Collect: 
• Surgical consent  
• Anaesthesia consent  
• Implant stickers (if applicable)  
Maintain: 
• OT Notes  
• Anaesthesia Record  
• Implant Utilization Record  
 
9. Billing Guidelines 
Bill Preparation Standards 
Bills must include: 
• Date-wise charges  
• Room rent  
• Nursing charges  
• Consultation fees  
• Pharmacy charges  
• Diagnostics

• Procedures  
 
Non-Payable Items 
Separate identification required for: 
• Registration charges  
• Food for attendants  
• Toiletries  
• Telephone charges  
• Visitor consumables  
Patient should be informed before discharge. 
 
10. Discharge Process 
Pre-Discharge Checklist 
Insurance Desk shall verify: 
• Final bill completed  
• Discharge summary prepared  
• Final authorization requested  
• Query responses submitted  
 
Final Authorization Request 
Documents required: 
1. Final bill  
2. Break-up bill  
3. Discharge summary  
4. Investigation reports  
5. OT notes (if surgery)  
6. Implant invoice  
7. Pharmacy statement  
Timeline: 
At least 4 hours before planned discharge.

11. Discharge Summary Requirements 
Must include: 
Patient Information 
• Name  
• UHID  
• Age/Gender  
Clinical Details 
• Admission diagnosis  
• Final diagnosis  
• Procedures performed  
• Treatment provided  
Outcome 
• Condition at discharge  
• Medication advice  
• Follow-up instructions  
Authentication 
• Consultant signature  
• Hospital seal  
 
12. Claims Documentation Checklist 
Mandatory Documents 
Medical 
• Admission note  
• Progress sheets  
• Nursing records  
• Investigation reports  
• Procedure records  
Financial 
• Final bill

• Receipt  
• Pharmacy invoices  
• Implant invoices  
Administrative 
• Insurance card copy  
• ID proof  
• Claim forms  
 
13. Query Management 
TPA Query Response SLA 
Query Type Response Time 
Clinical Query 4 Hours 
Billing Query 4 Hours 
Document Query 2 Hours 
Discharge Query 1 Hour 
Escalation required beyond SLA. 
 
14. Fraud, Waste & Abuse Controls 
Hospital staff shall identify: 
Fraud Indicators 
• Identity mismatch  
• Fabricated documents  
• Inflated billing  
• Unnecessary admissions  
• Unbundling of procedures  
Reporting 
All suspected fraud must be reported to: 
• Hospital Compliance Officer  
• Medi Assist Fraud Control Unit  
Within 24 hours.

15. Data Privacy & Security 
Hospital shall comply with: 
• Digital Personal Data Protection Act (India)  
• IRDAI Guidelines  
• Hospital Information Security Policies  
Patient information shall: 
• Be accessed only by authorized personnel  
• Be encrypted during transmission  
• Not be shared through personal email or messaging applications  
 
16. Record Retention 
Document Type Retention Period 
Medical Records 10 Years 
Claims Records 10 Years 
Billing Records 8 Years 
Audit Records 10 Years 
 
17. Audit Requirements 
Hospital shall permit: 
• Clinical audits  
• Billing audits  
• Documentation audits  
• Fraud investigations  
Audit observations must be closed within 30 days.

Pre-auth Submission ≤ 2 Hours

Claim Rejection Rate < 2% 
Documentation Completeness > 98% 
Fraud Incidents 0
